  "title": "Commitment Depth Routing: Selective Video Activation in Video-Action Models",
  "core_problem": "Video-Action Models (VAMs) like mimic-video train their action decoder robust to any τ_v ∈ [0,1] via logit-normal sampling, making τ_v a flexible test-time parameter. A foundational verified finding from mimic-video (arXiv:2512.15692): τ_v=1 (pure noise video input, single backbone forward pass) is the best single global default on SIMPLER-Bridge, achieving 46.9% task success. This is consistent with Fast-WAM (arXiv:2603.16666), which achieves 97.6% LIBERO by skipping test-time future video generation entirely. Critically, τ_v=0 (fully denoised video) gives WORSE autonomous policy performance than intermediate τ_v values — a fact that invalidated CDR's prior Phase 1 reference (which incorrectly targeted τ_v=0) and must be incorporated into any τ_v routing method. Yet mimic-video's per-task τ_v sweep yields +9.4pp on SIMPLER-Bridge (46.9%→56.3%), proving that SOME tasks genuinely benefit from actual video denoising (τ_v < 1). The core gap is a selective video activation problem: which observations within which tasks need video denoising below τ_v=1, and can this be predicted zero-shot without expensive per-task offline rollouts?

Existing approaches are non-adaptive: (1) LingBot-VA (RSS 2026) fixes τ_v≈0.6 uniformly — imposes video denoising costs even where τ_v=1 suffices and may misallocate compute away from phases where a different threshold is optimal; (2) Fast-WAM skips video entirely via architectural retraining — effective on average but permanently loses gains for tasks where video is genuinely critical; (3) mimic-video's per-task sweeping requires ~10 rollouts per new task at deployment time. No system selectively activates video denoising only for observations where it materially improves action quality relative to the globally optimal τ_v=1 default, and no paper has empirically studied which manipulation phases within 3D episodes benefit from τ_v < 1. CDR addresses this: default to τ_v=1 everywhere, activate video denoising (route to τ_v < 1) only when predicted necessary, recover per-task sweep gains without offline rollouts.",
  "opportunity": "The key enabling property is mimic-video's variable-τ_v training (logit-normal over [0,1]), which makes the action decoder robust at τ_v=1 (globally optimal, safe default) while also capable of exploiting richer video features at lower τ_v. CDR exploits this asymmetry: a lightweight router that defaults to τ_v=1 — the globally optimal and compute-efficient choice — and activates actual video denoising (routes to τ_v < 1) only for observations where the action decoder's output demonstrably benefits from real video structure, as measured by proximity to ground-truth demonstration actions.

The inverted framing from prior CDR is essential: τ_v=1 is NOT the 'coarse shortcut' that precision phases must escape — it IS the globally correct starting point. CDR asks: 'which frames are exceptions to the τ_v=1 global optimum, and can we learn to identify them?' The per-task sweep gain (+9.4pp) proves exceptions exist at task scale; CDR's Phase 1 study asks whether they cluster in specific manipulation phases (grasp, insert) within tasks.

Two publishable outcomes with asymmetric CoRL value: (1) If per-observation τ_v* < 1 frames concentrate in precision phases with >2pp per-phase improvement: CDR demonstrates selective video activation as a Pareto-superior alternative to both Fast-WAM (universal skip) and LingBot-VA (universal partial denoising) — the router outperforms both fixed baselines on the task-success vs. mean-τ_v-consumed Pareto frontier, on SIMPLER-Bridge. (2) If within-task per-phase variation is small (<2pp): task-level CDR router recovers ≥80% of per-task sweep gain (+7.5pp of +9.4pp) zero-shot on SIMPLER-Bridge — a concrete deployment contribution automating mimic-video's expensive per-task offline sweep via a frozen MLP trained on LIBERO-100 task embeddings. Outcome 2 must be framed with specific numerical targets (≥80% recovery) to meet CoRL bar; 'validation study alone' is insufficient.",
  "landscape": "LingBot-VA (arXiv:2601.21998, RSS 2026, Ant Group) is CDR's primary comparison. Noisy History Augmentation (saug ∈ [0.5,1.0] during training) enables fixed 3-step inference to s=0.6. Key distinction from CDR: LingBot-VA imposes a LOWER τ_v (more denoising) than the globally optimal τ_v=1 uniformly across all frames, assuming this universally improves performance. CDR's critical empirical test: is uniform τ_v=0.6 better or worse than selective activation (default τ_v=1, activate only when predicted necessary)? If CDR matches LingBot-VA's performance at lower mean τ_v consumed, or exceeds LingBot-VA on precision tasks where the optimal activation threshold differs from 0.6, CDR demonstrates a Pareto-superior operating point. 98.5% LIBERO (Spatial 98.5, Object 99.6, Goal 97.2, Long 98.5), 92.2% RoboTwin. No per-phase analysis; fixed threshold assumed without verification.

mimic-video (arXiv:2512.15692, Dec 2025) is CDR's base model. Verified key findings: (a) τ_v=1 is explicitly the best single global default on SIMPLER-Bridge ('a good default value that balances policy performance and inference speed'); (b) per-task sweep yields +9.4pp (46.9%→56.3%); (c) τ_v=0 gives WORSE performance than intermediate τ_v. These three findings collectively define CDR's corrected premise: start from τ_v=1, activate selectively based on GT action quality, never route toward τ_v=0. 93.9% LIBERO, 46.9%/56.3% SIMPLER-Bridge.

Fast-WAM (arXiv:2603.16666, Mar 2026) removes test-time future video prediction by processing only the first clean observation frame — architecturally different from τ_v=1 (which passes noisy future frames through the full backbone). 97.6% LIBERO, 91.8% RoboTwin, 4× speedup; requires retraining. CDR is post-hoc (no backbone retraining) and occupies the selective middle: defer to Fast-WAM-style efficiency (τ_v=1) by default, activate actual video generation for precision-critical frames.

VADF: Vision-Adaptive Diffusion Policy Framework (arXiv:2604.15938, Apr 2026) adapts ACTION diffusion denoising steps per task stage via a Hierarchical Vision Task Segmenter — orthogonal to CDR. VADF modifies the action diffusion process (fewer steps for simple actions, more for complex); CDR modifies the VIDEO backbone denoising depth (τ_v). These address different computational bottlenecks and can be combined. VADF is evaluated on simpler manipulation setups (Push-T, Adroit, ARX5); CDR targets WAM-class models on SIMPLER-Bridge and LIBERO-100.

DiT4DiT (arXiv:2603.10448) ablation: single-step (high τ_v) is best on average — independently confirms τ_v=1 global optimality, supporting CDR's corrected framing. 98.6% LIBERO, 50.8% RoboCasa. DreamZero (arXiv:2602.15922, Feb 2026, 14B WAM) caches velocity within a denoising trajectory; complementary to CDR (reduces cost within given τ_v level vs. CDR choosing the τ_v level). ChEaP (arXiv:2603.30043) establishes early plan commitment in 2D mazes (first few denoising steps commit high-level motion; further steps add visual detail only); CDR empirically validates and extends this to 3D manipulation video backbones. 'Denoising, Fast and Slow' (CVPR 2026, arXiv:2604.19141) motivates per-sample difficulty routing in image diffusion — supports CDR's feasibility argument. D3P (arXiv:2508.06804) adapts ACTION denoising steps via RL — complementary efficiency axis (same as VADF, different mechanism). X-WAM (arXiv:2604.26694) uses Asynchronous Noise Sampling from a fixed joint distribution — not per-observation adaptive. UWM (arXiv:2504.02792) uses independent modality timesteps from fixed schedule. Being-H0.7 (arXiv:2605.00078) avoids pixel decoding via distillation. S-VAM (arXiv:2603.16195) distills multi-step to one-step; requires retraining. 'When to Trust Imagination' (arXiv:2605.06222) reduces replanning frequency; orthogonal to per-call CDR.

No existing VAM paper: (a) uses GT-action-referenced τ_v labeling (correcting the τ_v=0 reference error); (b) studies which 3D manipulation phases need τ_v < 1 empirically; or (c) trains a zero-shot per-task/per-observation τ_v predictor that generalizes across tasks without offline rollouts.",
  "approach": "CDR has four sequenced phases relative to a deployed mimic-video checkpoint (no backbone retraining required):

**Phase 0 — Sanity Check (1–2 H100-hours, PREREQUISITE, run immediately):**
Take 5 LIBERO tasks spanning types (2 precision grasp/insert, 2 pick-and-place, 1 long-horizon). Run 3 demonstration trajectories each (~1,500 frames total). Sweep τ_v ∈ {1.0, 0.9, ..., 0.1} using the frozen mimic-video action decoder. Compute τ_v*(f) = argmin_{τ_v ∈ {1.0,...,0.1}} ||a_{τ_v}(f) − a_GT(f)||₂ for each frame f (GT action from demo teleop). Annotate frames by manipulation phase using end-effector distance to target + gripper state.

Decision gate (by May 12):
- If <10% of frames have τ_v* < 0.9 (nearly all frames prefer τ_v=1 for action quality): per-observation variation is minimal. Pivot paper framing to 'τ_v=1 universality study + automated zero-shot per-task routing' — do NOT commit to full Phase 1 scope. Reframe contribution as empirical validation + deployment automation.
- If ≥20% of frames have τ_v* < 0.9 AND these cluster in grasp/insert phases: full CDR selective activation story is empirically supported. Proceed to Phase 1.
- Intermediate (10–20%): assess within-episode vs. across-task variance before proceeding.

**Phase 1 — 3D Video Necessity Study (~40–60 H100-hours):**
[CORRECTED REFERENCE — CRITICAL FIX] For each frame f in LIBERO-100 (100 tasks × 50 demos × ~100 steps ≈ 500K frames), compute:

  τ_v*(f) = argmin_{τ_v ∈ {1.0, 0.9, ..., 0.1}} ||a_{τ_v}(f) − a_GT(f)||₂

where a_GT(f) is the ground-truth demonstration action at frame f (available from LIBERO-100 teleop data) and a_{τ_v}(f) is the mimic-video action decoder output with τ_v-noised video input. This replaces the prior critically flawed reference (τ_v=0, which mimic-video shows is empirically worse than intermediate τ_v for autonomous policy performance). The sweep range {1.0,...,0.1} excludes τ_v=0 entirely.

Annotate frames with manipulation phases: approach (end-effector distance > 5cm to target), pre-grasp (distance 1–5cm, gripper open), grasp (gripper closing event), transport (gripper closed, object moving), place (object near target, gripper opening). Derive from proprioceptive state; no additional network required.

Report: (a) Distribution of τ_v* — specifically fraction of frames where τ_v*=1.0 (no activation needed) vs. τ_v* < 0.9; (b) Mean τ_v* by manipulation phase — do grasp/insert phases have significantly lower τ_v* than approach/transport? (c) Within-episode τ_v* variance vs. across-task τ_v* variance — which dominates? (d) Whether LingBot-VA's fixed s≈0.6 corresponds to over-denoising for approach frames and potentially misaligned thresholds for other phases.

[Distribution shift mitigation]: Include suboptimal rollout states to reduce demo-vs-rollout gap. Specifically: run the mimic-video policy (τ_v=1) 3× per task on LIBERO-100, collect frames from failed/recovery trajectories (partial grasps, dropped objects, recovery approaches). Add these to the labeling dataset (~50% of total labeled frames from non-expert trajectories). This gives the router diverse training states including recovery behaviors seen during closed-loop evaluation.

Compute: ~750K frames × 10 τ_v levels = ~7.5M backbone forward passes. With batch=64 on Cosmos-Predict2 (2B DiT), ~40–60 H100-hours.

**Phase 2 — Router Training (~5 H100-hours):**
[SIMPLIFIED vs. prior CDR] 4-class router instead of 10-class: {τ_v=1.0 (no activation), τ_v∈[0.7,0.9] (light activation), τ_v∈[0.4,0.6] (medium activation), τ_v∈[0.1,0.3] (heavy activation)}. Labels from Phase 1 mapped to nearest class bin. Architecture: two-layer MLP (512-dim CLIP image embedding + 512-dim frozen mimic-video language embedding → 256-dim hidden ReLU → 4-class softmax). Loss: CE(τ̂, τ_v*_class) + λ·E[τ̂_consumed].

Conservative routing (addressing distribution shift): if max softmax probability < θ, predict τ_v=1.0 regardless of argmax — since τ_v=1 is globally optimal, falling back to it on uncertain (OOD) states is safe. Sweep λ ∈ {0.01, 0.1, 0.5} and θ ∈ {0.5, 0.7, 0.9} to trace the accuracy-efficiency frontier.

Task-level CDR variant: also train on task-mean τ_v* (average τ_v* across all frames in a task) to enable the per-task routing baseline (d) and test zero-shot generalization on SIMPLER-Bridge.

**Phase 3 — Evaluation (~50 H100-hours, primary benchmark: SIMPLER-Bridge):**

Baselines:
(a) mimic-video τ_v=1 global (globally optimal default, 46.9% SIMPLER, 93.9% LIBERO)
(b) LingBot-VA-style fixed τ_v=0.5 on mimic-video base (primary CDR comparison — tests whether uniform partial denoising beats selective activation)
(c) LingBot-VA-style fixed τ_v=0.7, 0.9 sweep (find fixed-threshold Pareto frontier for fair comparison)
(d) Per-task CDR router (predict task-mean τ_v* zero-shot on SIMPLER-Bridge — primary fallback result; claim: recovers ≥80% of +9.4pp sweep gain = ≥7.5pp without offline rollouts)
(e) Per-observation CDR (full system)
(f) Per-task sweep oracle (56.3% SIMPLER — upper bound)

Primary results: Pareto curves (task success vs. mean τ_v consumed) on SIMPLER-Bridge. LIBERO-100 results reported secondarily for comparability. Key empirical claims:
1. Per-observation CDR Pareto-dominates all fixed-threshold baselines (b,c) on SIMPLER-Bridge — or if not, per-task CDR does
2. Per-task CDR recovers ≥80% of per-task sweep gain zero-shot on SIMPLER-Bridge
3. CDR allocates lower τ_v (more video activation) to grasp-phase frames than approach frames — interpretability via per-phase τ_v heatmaps

Ablations: per-phase τ_v allocation analysis (grasp vs. approach); precision task subset (peg insertion, mug hanging) vs. coarse tasks; conservative routing ablation (θ sweep); zero-shot generalization from LIBERO-100 router to SIMPLER-Bridge tasks (no retraining — key deployment story).

Note on absolute LIBERO numbers: CDR built on mimic-video (93.9%) will fall below LingBot-VA (98.5%) and DiT4DiT (98.6%) due to base model gap. Paper leads with SIMPLER-Bridge Pareto curves in abstract/intro. LIBERO results in supplementary for comparability. This framing is explicitly stated in introduction: 'Our contribution is the selective activation principle and zero-shot deployment, not absolute SOTA on LIBERO.'

**Timeline for CoRL 2026 (May 29 deadline):**
- Phase 0: run May 10–11 (1–2 H100-hours, 1–2 days)

- Phase 1 (if positive): May 12–18 (40–60h, with 8 H100s = 5–8 days)
- Phase 2: May 18–19 (~1 day)
- Phase 3: May 19–25 (50h / 8 H100s = ~6 days)
- Write-up: May 25–28 (4 days)
- Buffer: May 29 submission

## Reviewer feedback (round 4)
Issues: ["MODERATE — Fast-WAM SIMPLER-Bridge gap: Fast-WAM (arXiv:2603.16666) reports results only on LIBERO and RoboTwin in the abstract and appears not to evaluate on SIMPLER-Bridge. The proposal's Phase 3 plans to compare CDR against a 'Fast-WAM-style' baseline on SIMPLER-Bridge but this requires either (a) running Fast-WAM's architecture on mimic-video's SIMPLER-Bridge setup or (b) using τ_v=1 as a proxy for Fast-WAM's behavior — the proposal conflates these. τ_v=1 in mimic-video is NOT architecturally equivalent to Fast-WAM: τ_v=1 still processes noisy future frames through the full backbone, while Fast-WAM modifies architecture to not generate future frames. The paper must clearly state which 'Fast-WAM-style' baseline is being run and how it is implemented on the mimic-video backbone.", "MODERATE — 'Denoising, Fast and Slow' mischaracterized as 'per-sample difficulty routing': WebFetch of arXiv:2604.19141 confirms this CVPR 2026 paper does PATCH-LEVEL spatial routing within images (varying timesteps across image regions), NOT per-sample routing across observations in a trajectory. The proposal describes it as 'per-sample difficulty routing in image diffusion — supports CDR's feasibility argument.' This mischaracterization is relatively minor but CoRL reviewers familiar with the paper will catch it. More importantly, the differentiation from CDR is actually cleaner than the proposal implies: CDR is temporal routing across trajectory timesteps; 'Denoising Fast and Slow' is spatial routing across image patches. The proposal should make this distinction explicit.", "MODERATE — τ_v=1 global optimality claim is stated as 'foundational verified' but the WebFetch of the mimic-video HTML only confirmed that the scratch (no per-task tuning) result is 46.9%, not that τ_v=1 specifically is the best single fixed τ_v among all possible fixed values. The paper states 'performance peaks at an INTERMEDIATE noise level' per-task; if a fixed global τ_v=0.8 outperforms τ_v=1 on SIMPLER-Bridge aggregate, CDR's 'τ_v=1 as globally optimal default' framing collapses. This must be verified from Table I or Figure 5 of mimic-video before committing to this framing.", "MODERATE — 20-day critical path has zero slack for Phase 1 overruns: Phase 0 decision on May 12 + Phase 1 (5–8 days on 8 H100s) + Phase 2 (1 day) + Phase 3 (6 days) + Writing (4 days) = 16–19 days to May 28-29 submission. If Phase 1 takes 8 days (upper bound of 60h / 8 GPUs), writing is compressed to 2 days or Phase 3 is cut. The proposal should explicitly acknowledge that Phase 3 ablations (RoboCasa, per-phase heatmaps) are drop-able if Phase 1 runs long, and that the minimum viable submission needs only SIMPLER-Bridge primary results.", "MINOR — MotuBrain (arXiv:2604.27792) is unaddressed: MotuBrain biases video timestep sampling toward noisier regions during training to improve robustness under noisy visual conditions — this is related to CDR's study of τ_v sensitivity. While MotuBrain is a training-time technique and CDR is a test-time router, reviewers may conflate them. CDR's landscape should acknowledge MotuBrain briefly as a training-time complementary approach vs. CDR's test-time routing.", "MINOR — SIMPLER-Bridge is mimic-video's primary benchmark but is not universally known in the CoRL community: if the majority of reviewers are primarily familiar with LIBERO (the most common WAM benchmark), leading with SIMPLER-Bridge scores (where CDR's base 46.9% looks weak in absolute terms) may create a poor first impression. The abstract should explicitly state '46.9% is the state-of-the-art on this task for models of this size' or note that SIMPLER-Bridge is evaluation on real-to-sim transfer tasks where most methods score <55%."]
Feedback: Round 4 correctly resolves all Round 3 critical issues: the τ_v=0 reference has been replaced with GT actions (||a_{τ_v} − a_GT||₂), τ_v=1 is reframed as globally optimal default, distribution shift is mitigated via 50% non-expert rollout states, Phase 0 is a proper gate, and the fallback has concrete numerical targets (≥80% sweep gain recovery). The proposal is now scientifically sound and structurally well-organized. Three focused fixes are needed for Round 5:

**Fix 1 (highest priority — 30 min)**: Verify from mimic-video Table I / Figure 5 that τ_v=1.0 specifically is the best among ALL fixed τ_v values globally (not just 'no per-task tuning').
